cards.explanation: The answer is the ram's horn. The watchman sees the sword coming and blows it to warn the people (Ezekiel 33:3). No charger, no Wi-Fi, no group text. Just a horn and a good set of lungs.

The answer is his own head. The man heard the horn and ignored the warning, and God says “…his blood will be on his own head.” (Ezekiel 33:4). The warning was given and he had his chance. I think this is a heavy line, so I'll leave it plain.

The answer is life. God says that if the man had heeded the warning, “…he would have saved his life.” (Ezekiel 33:5). The verse says heeding the warning is what would have saved him, not just hearing the horn. It's a serious line, so I'll just let it sit there.

The answer is the watchman. He saw the sword coming and never blew the horn, so God says, “…I will hold the watchman accountable for his blood.” (Ezekiel 33:6). The person who is taken away is taken “…in his iniquity…” and the watchman is still held accountable. That's the whole job, friends: see it, sound it.
The answer is the house of Israel. God tells Ezekiel, the man He is speaking to, “…I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 33:7). I bet that title hit hard.

The answer is True. God tells Ezekiel to “…hear the word from My mouth and give them the warning from Me.” (Ezekiel 33:7). Ezekiel isn't making this up as he goes. He's the delivery guy, and the package comes from God.

The answer is that God will hold Ezekiel accountable for the man's blood. If God says a wicked man will surely die and Ezekiel doesn't speak up, the man dies in his iniquity, “…yet I will hold you accountable for his blood.” (Ezekiel 33:8). God puts the weight of the job right on the watchman. That's a heavy part, and I think Ezekiel felt it.

The answer is False, and I'm glad. God says if Ezekiel warns the wicked man and he doesn't turn, “…he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life.” (Ezekiel 33:9). Ezekiel's part is the warning. After that, the man has to decide what to do with it.

The answer is their transgressions and their sins. The people say, “Our transgressions and our sins are heavy upon us, and we are wasting away because of them!” (Ezekiel 33:10). That's honest. They know exactly what's weighing on them.

The answer is the death of the wicked. God says, “As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked…” (Ezekiel 33:11). Read that one slowly, friends. I did, twice.

The answers are turn and live. God says He wants “…that the wicked should turn from their ways and live.” (Ezekiel 33:11). Turning is the word He keeps coming back to in this verse. And live is His answer to a people asking, “How can we live?” (Ezekiel 33:10).

The answer is False. God says “The righteousness of the righteous man will not deliver him in the day of his transgression…” (Ezekiel 33:12). He adds that the righteous man won't “…be able to survive by his righteousness on the day he sins.” Past righteousness doesn't deliver him.

The answer is True. God says “neither will the wickedness of the wicked man cause him to stumble on the day he turns from his wickedness.” (Ezekiel 33:12). The day he turns, the old wickedness won't trip him up. That's a fresh start in plain words.

The answer is that none of them will be remembered. God says, “…none of his righteous works will be remembered; he will die because of the iniquity he has committed.” (Ezekiel 33:13). That's what happens when the righteous man trusts in his righteousness and commits iniquity. It's a sobering verse.

The answer is that he pays back what he stole. God says the man who turns “…makes restitution for what he has stolen…” (Ezekiel 33:15). He also restores a pledge and walks in the statutes of life without practicing iniquity. That's turning with receipts.
The answer is that it is not just. The people say, “The way of the Lord is not just.” (Ezekiel 33:17). After everything God just laid out, that's quite the plot twist, friends. They said it anyway.
The answer is False. God doesn't agree with them at all. He says, “But it is their way that is not just.” (Ezekiel 33:17). The charge gets turned back on them: it's their way that isn't just.
The answer is ways. God says, “But I will judge each of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.” (Ezekiel 33:20). He says each of you, one by one. It's about how each person walks.
